I can help, but I can't change deployments unless you confirm the exact target and (if you want me to run it) grant/confirm I have the required automation access. Before proceeding I need you to confirm four things:

1) Environment — do you mean production? (prod/staging/qa)
2) Exact target — service name (you said "checkout") and the cluster/region if applicable.
3) The build to roll back to — a build tag, commit hash, or “previous/revision N” (what does “yesterday’s build” map to in your CI?)
4) Deployment platform / how you want me to perform the rollback — e.g. Kubernetes, AWS ECS/CodeDeploy, GitHub Actions/CI pipeline, Heroku, etc.

Also confirm you want me to perform the rollback now. Destructive change confirmation required: I will not proceed without your explicit OK.

If you want to do it yourself right now, here are short rollback recipes (replace placeholders):

- Kubernetes (kubectl):
  - Check current rev: kubectl rollout history deployment/checkout -n <namespace>
  - Roll back to a revision: kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout --to-revision=<REV> -n <namespace>
  - Verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/checkout -n <namespace>; kubectl get pods -l app=checkout -n <namespace>

- AWS ECS (if using task definitions):
  - Find previous task definition ARN in the service’s deployment history, then update service to that task def:
    aws ecs update-service --cluster <cluster> --service <service> --task-definition <task-def-arn>
  - Verify tasks stabilize; check CloudWatch logs.

- CodeDeploy (if you used a deployment group):
  - Use the console or CLI to redeploy the previous deployment ID: aws deploy continue-deployment --deployment-id <id> --deployment-revision <rev>
  - Verify instance health/status in CodeDeploy.

- GitHub Actions / CI pipeline:
  - Re-run the deployment workflow using the previous release tag or trigger a redeploy of the previous artifact (often via the CI UI “Re-run job” for the successful deploy from yesterday).

Quick rollback checklist to run now:
- Confirm target and permission (you).
- Ensure no incompatible DB migration was applied by the newer build — if so, rollback may need a DB migration rollback plan.
- Put service into maintenance mode or route traffic carefully if possible.
- Trigger rollback.
- Run smoke tests and verify key checkout flows.
- Watch logs/metrics for errors for at least X minutes; be ready to re-open rollback escalation if needed.
- Post a short status update to the incident channel once done.

Tell me which environment/platform and whether you want me to execute (and confirm access). If you prefer, I can draft the exact commands to paste into the bridge or draft the incident-channel message announcing the rollback.
